chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Teacher P. B. Langford from St. Louis
summary: Thomas praises Langford, a professional musician who came out from St. Louis, could relate to kids, taught every band instrument, and was honored by Sousa.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Now, you want me to talk to you about Mr. Sims. His idea to get the kids together, keep them out of trouble, you know. I don't know what kind of trouble we could have gotten into in Webster Groves because that's a long time ago, you know. ...
(both talking)
So, he got this band together. I think I must have been, Stan, well, around 8 years old and he found a very fine teacher. I always think he's one of the finest, Mr. P. B. Langford.
Oh, yeah.
JT THOMAS (1) 4
Yeah, tremendous, out of St. Louis, tremendous teacher.
How far from St. Louis was Webster Groves?
I would think about 12 miles.
Well, that was really quite handy.
Well, handy for the kids because we could take a little car ride and get into town.
How do you spell Langford?
D: This has it L-dnk...
L-a-n-g-f-o-r-d. And a tremendous man. The man knew, the teacher knew how to handle kids. The word they use now is relate. Well, he could relate to kids. And the kids loved him.
What did he do, was that his living? Was he a teacher by profession?

Well, he was a teacher by profession, a professional allowed musician. A tremendous musician and he allowed us a certain amount of leniency. There was, I mean there's baseball and all those things and he was patient enough, he called the time but he was patient enough to give you a break of 5 or 10 minutes sun is before it happened. You know, sunshine shining, too. And he was a tremendous teacher. He has written some things, Sousa had honored him by doing one of his marches and I can't remember just what one of the marches it was. Tremendous musician.
Do you know where he was educated at all?
JTHOMAS (1)
No, I don't.
Because he must have had, he must have been a well-schooled musician originally.

Tremendous. He played everything. He's a tremendous musician. He played the trumpet, the cornet rather but he could instruct the trombone, the clarinet, the drums. Yes, he's a tremendous musician and a tremendous person. And he could impart what he wanted to impart to you.
Which is something else. Without
Without making you feel dumb, you know.
Yeah.
Which we were. Yeah, we were
